data.name: Day 1 - Container
data.description:
Container
The Container widget is one of the most commonly used and powerful widgets in Flutter. It acts as a box model that helps in designing layouts by combining multiple properties into a single widget.

🔹 What can Container do?

Add padding & margin

Set width & height

Apply background color or gradient

Add borders & rounded corners

Apply box shadow

Align child widgets

🔹 Why Container is important?
Instead of nesting multiple widgets like Padding, Align, DecoratedBox, etc., Container simplifies UI design by handling them in one place.🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Cards
✅ Buttons
✅ Layout blocks
✅ Profile avatars
✅ Custom UI components

💡 Mastering Container helps you understand Flutter layout fundamentals.

data.name: Day 2 - Row
data.description:
Row
The Row widget is used to arrange its child widgets horizontally in Flutter. It is one of the core layout widgets and forms the foundation of responsive UI design.

🔹 What does Row do?

Lays out widgets from left to right

Controls spacing and alignment of children

Helps build toolbars, menus, buttons, and forms

🔹 Key properties:

children – widgets inside the Row

mainAxisAlignment – horizontal alignment

crossAxisAlignment – vertical alignment

mainAxisSize – how much horizontal space Row occupies🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ App bars
✅ Icon + text layouts
✅ Action buttons
✅ Horizontal lists

💡 Mastering Row helps you fully understand Flutter’s layout system.

data.name: Day 3 - Column
data.description:
Column
The Column widget is used to arrange its child widgets vertically in Flutter. It is a fundamental layout widget that helps structure screens from top to bottom.

🔹 What does Column do?

Lays out widgets vertically

Controls spacing and alignment of children

Helps build forms, lists, sections, and stacked UI elements

🔹 Key properties:

children – widgets inside the Column

mainAxisAlignment – vertical alignment

crossAxisAlignment – horizontal alignment

mainAxisSize – how much vertical space the Column occupies🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Forms
✅ Profile sections
✅ Settings screens
✅ Vertical menus

💡 Understanding Column along with Row gives you full control over Flutter layouts.

data.name: Day 4 - Stack
data.description:
Stack
The Stack widget allows you to overlay widgets on top of each other, making it perfect for layered UI designs and custom layouts.

🔹 What does Stack do?

Places widgets on top of one another

Supports absolute positioning using Positioned

Enables complex UI designs with depth and layering

🔹 Key properties:

children – widgets inside the Stack

alignment – default alignment of children

fit – how non-positioned children are sized

clipBehavior – controls overflow clipping🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Profile images with badges
✅ Floating buttons
✅ Image overlays
✅ Custom cards and banners

💡 Stack gives you creative freedom to build visually rich and layered UIs.

data.name: Day 5 - Text
data.description:
Text
The Text widget is used to display strings of text in Flutter. It is one of the most basic yet essential widgets for building readable and user-friendly UIs.

🔹 What does Text do?

Displays single or multiple lines of text

Supports rich styling and alignment

Handles overflow, wrapping, and scaling

🔹 Key properties:

style – font size, weight, color, font family

textAlign – alignment of text

maxLines – limits number of lines

overflow – handles text overflow

softWrap – wraps text to next line🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Titles & headings
✅ Labels & descriptions
✅ Buttons & menus
✅ Error and status messages

💡 Mastering the Text widget helps you build clean, accessible, and polished UIs.
data.code:
Text(
  'Flutter Text Widget',
  style: TextStyle(
    fontSize: 18,
    fontWeight: FontWeight.bold,
    color: Colors.blue,
  ),
  textAlign: TextAlign.center,
  maxLines: 2,
  overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
);

data.name: Day 6 - Image
data.description:
Image
The Image widget is used to display images in Flutter applications. It supports multiple image sources and provides full control over sizing, fitting, and alignment.

🔹 What does Image do?

Displays images from assets, network, files, or memory

Controls how images fit within their bounds

Supports placeholders and error handling

🔹 Key properties:

image / Image.asset, Image.network

fit – controls how the image fits (cover, contain, fill, etc.)

width & height – size of the image

alignment – image alignment within its bounds

color & colorBlendMode – apply color effects🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Profile pictures
✅ Banners & thumbnails
✅ Product images
✅ Background visuals

💡 Mastering the Image widget helps you build visually rich and engaging Flutter UIs.

data.name: Day 7 - ListView
data.description:
ListView
The ListView widget is used to display a scrollable list of widgets in Flutter. It is essential for building dynamic and data-driven UIs that handle large amounts of content efficiently.

🔹 What does ListView do?

Displays items in a scrollable vertical or horizontal list

Lazily loads widgets for better performance

Supports separators, builders, and custom layouts

🔹 Common constructors:

ListView() – static list

ListView.builder() – dynamic, lazy-loaded list

ListView.separated() – list with separators

ListView.custom() – fully customized behavior🔹 Key properties:

scrollDirection – vertical or horizontal

physics – scroll behavior

shrinkWrap – size based on content

padding – space around list items

🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Chat screens
✅ Feeds & timelines
✅ Settings pages
✅ Product lists

💡 ListView is the backbone of most Flutter apps that display scrolling content.

data.name: Day 8 - GridView
data.description:
GridView
The GridView widget is used to display items in a two-dimensional scrollable grid. It’s ideal when you want to show content in rows and columns instead of a single list.

🔹 What does GridView do?

Displays widgets in a grid layout

Supports vertical and horizontal scrolling

Efficiently handles large datasets

🔹 Common constructors:

GridView.count() – fixed number of columns

GridView.extent() – max item width

GridView.builder() – dynamic, lazy-loaded grid

GridView.custom() – fully customized grid🔹 Key properties:

crossAxisCount – number of columns

mainAxisSpacing – vertical spacing

crossAxisSpacing – horizontal spacing

childAspectRatio – width vs height ratio

🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Image galleries
✅ Product listings
✅ Dashboards
✅ Category grids

💡 Use GridView when content looks better in blocks rather than a vertical list.

data.name: Day 9 - Expanded
data.description:
Expanded
The Expanded widget is used to make a child of a Row, Column, or Flex expand and fill the available space. It helps create responsive layouts without hard-coding sizes.

🔹 What does Expanded do?

Takes up available free space

Works only inside Flex widgets (Row, Column, Flex)

Automatically adjusts layout based on screen size

🔹 Key properties:

child – widget to expand

flex – controls how much space to take compared to siblings🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Responsive rows & columns
✅ Equal-width buttons
✅ Flexible cards
✅ Adaptive layouts

💡 Expanded is essential for building flexible and responsive Flutter UIs.

data.name: Day 10 - Padding
data.description:
Padding
The Padding widget is used to add space around a widget by insetting its child. It helps improve UI readability and spacing without affecting the widget’s size directly.

🔹 What does Padding do?

Adds empty space inside the parent layout

Improves UI spacing and visual clarity

Makes layouts more readable and user-friendly

🔹 Key properties:

padding – defines space using EdgeInsets

EdgeInsets.all()

EdgeInsets.symmetric()

EdgeInsets.only()🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Text spacing
✅ Buttons & cards
✅ Form fields
✅ Clean UI layouts

💡 Good spacing is key to great UI, and Padding makes it effortless.

data.name: Day 11 - Align
data.description:
Align
The Align widget is used to position a child widget within its parent using alignment values. It gives precise control over where a widget appears inside available space.

🔹 What does Align do?

Positions a widget within its parent

Uses alignment values from -1.0 to 1.0

Works well for fine-grained UI positioning

🔹 Key properties:

alignment – position of the child

child – widget to align

widthFactor & heightFactor – size relative to child🔹 Common alignments:

Alignment.center

Alignment.topLeft

Alignment.bottomRight

🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Floating icons
✅ Badges on images
✅ Custom layouts
✅ Overlay elements

💡 Align is perfect when you need exact positioning without complex layouts.

data.name: Day 12 - SizedBox
data.description:
SizedBox
The SizedBox widget is used to add fixed spacing or define a specific width and height for a widget. It helps create clean and consistent layouts without extra complexity.

🔹 What does SizedBox do?

• Adds vertical or horizontal space between widgets
• Sets fixed width and/or height
• Improves layout readability

🔹 Key properties:

• width – sets horizontal size
• height – sets vertical size
• child – widget inside the SizedBox🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Spacing between widgets
✅ Fixed-size buttons or cards
✅ Cleaner layouts
✅ Replacing unnecessary padding

💡 SizedBox is a lightweight and effective way to control spacing and sizing in Flutter layouts.
data.code:
SizedBox(height: 16)

SizedBox(
  width: 100,
  height: 100,
  child: Container(color: Colors.blue),
)

data.name: Day 13 - ElevatedButton
data.description:
ElevatedButton
The ElevatedButton widget is a material design button used to trigger actions in a Flutter app. It comes with elevation, background color, and built-in press animations.

🔹 What does ElevatedButton do?

• Creates a clickable button with elevation
• Handles user interactions like taps
• Follows Material Design guidelines

🔹 Key properties:

• onPressed – callback when button is tapped
• child – widget inside the button
• style – customize color, shape, padding, elevation🔹 Common customizations:

• Background color
• Rounded corners
• Padding & elevation
• Disabled state

🔹 Real-world use cases:
✅ Form submission
✅ Login / Signup buttons
✅ Call-to-action buttons
✅ Navigation triggers

💡 ElevatedButton is the go-to widget for primary actions in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 14 - IconButton
data.description:
IconButton
The IconButton widget is a tappable icon used to trigger actions in a Flutter app. It’s commonly used for toolbar actions, navigation controls, and quick interactions.

🔹 What does IconButton do?

• Creates a clickable icon
• Handles user interactions
• Provides visual feedback on tap
• Saves space compared to regular buttons

🔹 Key properties:

• onPressed – callback when tapped
• icon – the icon widget
• tooltip – accessibility hint
• color – icon color
• iconSize – size of the icon🔹 Common use cases:
✅ AppBar actions
✅ Navigation buttons
✅ Like/Favorite buttons
✅ Settings icons
✅ Toolbars

💡 IconButton is perfect for compact actions where space and clarity matter.

data.name: Day 15 - FloatingActionButton
data.description:
FloatingActionButton
The FloatingActionButton (FAB) is a circular button used to trigger a primary or most important action in a Flutter screen. It usually floats above the UI and grabs user attention.

🔹 What does FloatingActionButton do?

• Highlights the primary action of a screen
• Floats above content for easy access
• Follows Material Design guidelines

🔹 Key properties:

• onPressed – callback when tapped
• child – icon or widget inside the button
• backgroundColor – button color
• elevation – shadow depth
• tooltip – accessibility hint🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Add new item
✅ Create post
✅ Compose message
✅ Primary screen action

💡 FloatingActionButton is best used for one clear and important action per screen.

data.name: Day 16 - TextField
data.description:
TextField
The TextField widget is used to take user input such as text, numbers, passwords, or emails. It’s one of the most essential widgets for forms and interactive apps.

🔹 What does TextField do?

• Allows users to enter text
• Supports validation and formatting
• Highly customizable UI and behavior

🔹 Key properties:

• controller – read/write input value
• decoration – label, hint, border, icons
• keyboardType – text, number, email, etc.
• obscureText – hide input (passwords)🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Login & signup forms
✅ Search bars
✅ Feedback & comments
✅ Profile editing

💡 TextField is the foundation of user interaction in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 17 - Form
data.description:
Form
The Form widget is used to group multiple input fields together and manage their validation and state in one place. It’s essential for building structured and reliable user input flows.

🔹 What does Form do?

Groups multiple form fields
Manages validation and saving logic
Works seamlessly with TextFormField
Helps maintain clean and scalable input handling

🔹 Key properties:

key – uniquely identifies the form
child – contains form fields
autovalidateMode – controls validation behavior
onWillPop – handle back navigation logic🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Login & signup screens
✅ Profile editing
✅ Payment forms
✅ Feedback & surveys

💡 Form keeps validation logic centralized and your UI clean — a must-have for real-world Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 18 - CheckBox
data.description:
Checkbox
The Checkbox widget is used to capture a true / false choice from the user. It’s commonly used for selections, preferences, and confirmations in Flutter apps.

🔹 What does Checkbox do?

• Lets users toggle between checked and unchecked states
• Works well with forms and settings screens
• Supports active, inactive, and disabled states

🔹 Key properties:

• value – current checked state (true / false)
• onChanged – callback when value changes
• activeColor – color when checked
• checkColor – color of the check mark🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Accept terms & conditions
✅ Settings toggles
✅ Multi-select lists
✅ Filters & preferences

💡 Checkbox is ideal when users need clear, simple binary choices.

data.name: Day 19 - Switch
data.description:
Switch
The Switch widget is used to toggle between ON and OFF states. It’s commonly used for settings, preferences, and feature enable/disable options in Flutter apps.

🔹 What does Switch do?

• Toggles between true and false
• Provides instant visual feedback
• Best suited for settings and preferences

🔹 Key properties:

• value – current state of the switch
• onChanged – callback when toggled
• activeColor – thumb color when ON
• activeTrackColor – track color when ON🔹 Common use cases:
✅ App settings
✅ Dark mode toggle
✅ Notifications enable/disable
✅ Feature flags

💡 Switch is perfect when users need to instantly turn a feature ON or OFF.

data.name: Day 20 - RadioListTile
data.description:
RadioListTile
The RadioListTile widget is used to select one option from a group of choices. It combines a radio button with text, making selections clear and user-friendly in Flutter apps.

🔹 What does RadioListTile do?

• Allows selecting only one value at a time
• Groups related options together
• Provides clear visual feedback

🔹 Key properties:

• value – value represented by this radio option
• groupValue – currently selected value
• onChanged – callback when selection changes
• title – main label text
• subtitle – secondary description (optional)
• activeColor – color of the selected radio🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Settings selection
✅ Language or theme choice
✅ Single-choice forms
✅ Preference screens

💡 RadioListTile is perfect when users must choose exactly one option from multiple choices.

data.name: Day 21 - Slider
data.description:
Slider
The Slider widget allows users to select a value from a continuous range by dragging a thumb along a track. It’s commonly used for adjusting levels or ranges in a smooth and intuitive way.

🔹 What does Slider do?

• Lets users pick a numeric value visually
• Supports continuous or discrete values
• Updates value in real time while dragging
• Provides smooth and modern UX

🔹 Key properties:

• value – current selected value
• onChanged – callback when value changes
• min – minimum value
• max – maximum value
• activeColor – color of selected track
• inactiveColor – color of unselected track🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Volume control
✅ Brightness adjustment
✅ Price or range selection
✅ Progress or level control

💡 Slider is perfect when users need to adjust a value quickly and visually.

data.name: Day 22 - Card
data.description:
Card
The Card widget is a Material Design component used to group related content inside a clean, elevated container. It helps create visually separated sections in your UI.

🔹 What does Card do?

• Displays content inside a rounded container
• Adds elevation (shadow) for depth
• Improves visual hierarchy
• Follows Material Design standards

🔹 Key properties:

• child – widget inside the card
• elevation – depth shadow of the card
• shape – rounded corners or custom borders
• margin – space around the card
• color – background color🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Product listings
✅ Profile details
✅ Dashboard sections
✅ Info & preview blocks

💡 Card is perfect for organizing content into clean, readable sections.

data.name: Day 23 - AlertDialog
data.description:
AlertDialog
The AlertDialog widget is used to show important information, confirmations, or actions that require user attention. It appears as a popup dialog above the current screen.

🔹 What does AlertDialog do?

• Displays modal popup messages
• Blocks interaction until dismissed
• Used for confirmations and warnings
• Helps guide user decisions

🔹 Key properties:

• title – dialog title widget
• content – main message or UI
• actions – buttons like OK / Cancel
• shape – customize dialog corners🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Delete confirmation
✅ Logout alerts
✅ Error messages
✅ Permission prompts

💡 AlertDialog is perfect when user confirmation or attention is required before proceeding.

data.name: Day 24 - BottomNavigationBar
data.description:
BottomNavigationBar
The BottomNavigationBar widget is used to display navigation items at the bottom of the screen. It helps users quickly switch between top-level views in an app.

🔹 What does BottomNavigationBar do?

• Displays multiple navigation destinations
• Allows quick switching between main screens
• Keeps navigation visible at all times
• Improves app usability and structure

🔹 Key properties:

• currentIndex – currently selected tab
• onTap – callback when an item is tapped
• items – list of navigation items
• type – fixed or shifting
• selectedItemColor – active item color🔹 Common use cases:
✅ App main navigation
✅ Dashboard tabs
✅ E-commerce apps
✅ Social media apps

💡 BottomNavigationBar is perfect for apps with multiple primary screens that users switch between frequently.

data.name: Day 25 - TabBar
data.description:
TabBar
The TabBar widget is used to display a horizontal set of tabs that allow users to switch between different views or sections within the same screen.

🔹 What does TabBar do?

• Displays multiple tabs in a row
• Allows quick navigation between views
• Works with TabBarView for smooth transitions
• Keeps UI clean and organized

🔹 Key properties:

• tabs – list of tab widgets
• controller – controls tab selection
• onTap – callback when a tab is selected
• indicatorColor – color of selected tab indicator
• labelColor – color of active tab🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Category switching
✅ Profile sections
✅ Settings screens
✅ Dashboard views

💡 TabBar is perfect when you need structured navigation within the same screen.

data.name: Day 26 - Drawer
data.description:
Drawer
The Drawer widget provides a side navigation panel that slides in from the left (or right). It’s commonly used to show navigation links, user info, and app-level actions.

🔹 What does Drawer do?

• Displays a hidden side menu
• Helps organize navigation items
• Saves screen space
• Improves app structure for complex apps

🔹 Key properties:

• child – main content inside the drawer
• backgroundColor – drawer background color
• elevation – shadow depth
• shape – rounded corners
• width – custom drawer width🔹 Common use cases:
✅ App navigation
✅ Profile & settings access
✅ Category lists
✅ Dashboard menus

💡 Drawer is perfect for apps with multiple screens and structured navigation.

data.name: Day 27 - AppBar
data.description:
AppBar
The AppBar widget is a Material Design app bar that appears at the top of the screen. It typically shows the title, navigation icon, and action buttons.

🔹 What does AppBar do?
• Displays a top navigation bar
• Shows screen title
• Supports action icons
• Handles navigation (back/menu)
• Provides consistent app structure

🔹 Key properties:
• title – Main text displayed in the center/left
• leading – Widget before the title (menu/back icon)
• actions – List of action widgets (icons/buttons)
• backgroundColor – AppBar color
• elevation – Shadow depth🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Screen titles
✅ Back navigation
✅ Menu drawer trigger
✅ Search & action buttons
✅ App-wide branding

💡 AppBar is essential for navigation and structure in almost every Flutter app.

data.name: Day 28 - PageView
data.description:
PageView
The PageView widget allows users to swipe between different screens or pages horizontally or vertically. It’s commonly used for onboarding screens, image sliders, and step-based forms.

🔹 What does PageView do?

• Enables swipeable page navigation
• Displays one page at a time
• Supports horizontal & vertical scrolling
• Can be controlled programmatically

🔹 Key properties:

• controller – controls the page position
• children – list of pages
• onPageChanged – callback when page changes
• scrollDirection – horizontal or vertical🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Onboarding screens
✅ Image sliders
✅ Tutorial flows
✅ Multi-step forms

💡 PageView is perfect for creating smooth swipe-based experiences in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 29 - FutureBuilder
data.description:
FutureBuilder
The FutureBuilder widget builds its UI based on the latest snapshot of interaction with a Future. It is commonly used when working with asynchronous data like API calls, databases, or background tasks.

🔹 What does FutureBuilder do?

• Listens to a Future
• Rebuilds UI when the Future completes
• Handles loading, success, and error states
• Provides snapshot of async result

🔹 Key properties:

• future – the async operation to execute
• builder – builds UI based on snapshot
• snapshot.data – returned data
• snapshot.error – error information
• connectionState – waiting, active, done🔹 Common use cases:
✅ API calls
✅ Fetching remote data
✅ Database queries
✅ Async initialization

💡 FutureBuilder is essential for handling async operations cleanly in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 30 - Wrap
data.description:
Wrap
The Wrap widget automatically wraps its children to the next line (or column) when there isn’t enough space. It’s perfect for responsive layouts like tags, chips, or dynamic buttons.

🔹 What does Wrap do?

• Arranges widgets in horizontal or vertical direction
• Moves items to next line when space runs out
• Supports spacing between items
• Creates responsive UI layouts

🔹 Key properties:

• direction – horizontal or vertical
• spacing – space between items
• runSpacing – space between lines
• alignment – alignment of children
• children – list of widgets

🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Tag lists
✅ Category chips
✅ Dynamic button groups
✅ Responsive UI sections

💡 Wrap is perfect for building flexible and adaptive layouts in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 31 - ClipRRect
data.description:
ClipRRect
The ClipRRect widget clips its child using a rounded rectangle. It’s commonly used to create rounded corners for images, containers, and cards.

🔹 What does ClipRRect do?

• Clips its child widget
• Applies rounded corners
• Supports custom border radius
• Helps create modern UI designs

🔹 Key properties:

• borderRadius – defines corner radius
• child – widget to be clipped
• clipBehavior – controls clipping behavior🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Rounded profile images
✅ Card UI designs
✅ Banner images
✅ Custom shaped containers

💡 ClipRRect is perfect for creating clean, modern rounded UI elements in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 32 - Divider
data.description:
Divider
The Divider widget is a simple horizontal line used to separate content in Flutter apps. It helps improve readability and structure in lists, forms, and layouts.

🔹 What does Divider do?

• Adds a horizontal separation line
• Improves visual hierarchy
• Customizable thickness & color
• Adds spacing between sections

🔹 Key properties:

• height – total space occupied by divider
• thickness – line thickness
• color – divider color
• indent – left spacing
• endIndent – right spacing🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Separating ListTiles
✅ Sectioning forms
✅ Menu organization
✅ Improving UI structure

💡 Divider is perfect for creating clean and well-structured layouts in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 33 - Visibility
data.description:
Visibility
The Visibility widget controls whether a widget is visible or hidden in the UI. It’s perfect for showing or hiding content dynamically without rebuilding complex layouts.

🔹 What does Visibility do?

• Shows or hides a widget
• Replaces hidden widget with another widget
• Can maintain size, state, and animation
• Helps build dynamic UI

🔹 Key properties:

• visible – whether the child is shown
• child – the widget to display
• replacement – widget shown when not visible
• maintainState – keeps widget state when hidden
• maintainSize – keeps layout space
• maintainAnimation – keeps animations running🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Conditional UI rendering
✅ Showing error messages
✅ Toggle password visibility
✅ Feature flag handling
✅ Role-based content display

💡 Visibility is perfect for dynamically controlling parts of your UI in Flutter apps.

data.name: Day 34 - Hero
data.description:
Hero
The Hero widget creates smooth shared-element transitions between two screens. It animates a widget from one route to another, making navigation feel seamless and professional.

🔹 What does Hero do?

• Creates shared element transitions
• Animates widgets between screens
• Improves navigation experience
• Adds smooth visual continuity

🔹 Key properties:

• tag – unique identifier to link two Hero widgets
• child – the widget to animate
• flightShuttleBuilder – custom transition animation
• placeholderBuilder – widget shown during animation
• transitionOnUserGestures – enables gesture-based transitions🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Image gallery transitions
✅ Profile picture expansion
✅ Product detail animations
✅ Card-to-detail screen transitions
✅ Smooth page navigation

💡 Hero is perfect for creating beautiful, fluid transitions that elevate your Flutter app’s user experience.

data.name: Day 35 - ListTile
data.description:
ListTile
The ListTile widget is a single fixed-height row that typically contains text and optional leading/trailing widgets. It’s commonly used in lists, settings screens, menus, and navigation drawers.

🔹 What does ListTile do?

• Displays structured row content
• Supports leading & trailing widgets
• Handles tap interactions
• Works perfectly inside ListView

🔹 Key properties:

• leading – widget before the title (icon/avatar)
• title – primary text
• subtitle – secondary text below title
• trailing – widget after the title (icon/switch)
• onTap – callback when tapped
• selected – highlights the tile🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Settings screens
✅ Navigation drawers
✅ Contact lists
✅ Chat previews
✅ Profile menus

💡 ListTile helps you build clean, consistent list-based UIs quickly in Flutter.

data.name: Day 36 - RichText
data.description:
RichText
The RichText widget allows you to display text with multiple styles in a single line or paragraph. It gives you full control over text formatting using TextSpan.

🔹 What does RichText do?

• Displays multi-styled text
• Combines different colors, sizes & weights
• Supports inline styling
• Enables clickable text spans

🔹 Key properties:

• text – the TextSpan tree
• TextSpan – styled text segment
• style – default text style
• children – nested TextSpans
• recognizer – handles tap gestures🔹 Common use cases:
✅ Highlighting keywords
✅ Terms & Conditions links
✅ Mixed text formatting
✅ Inline clickable text
✅ Styled chat messages

💡 RichText is perfect when you need advanced text styling beyond a simple Text widget.

data.name: Day 37 - DropdownButton
data.description:
DropdownButton
The DropdownButton widget allows users to select one value from a list of options. It displays the currently selected item and shows a dropdown menu when tapped.

🔹 What does DropdownButton do?

• Displays a list of selectable items
• Shows selected value
• Expands into a dropdown menu
• Handles selection changes

🔹 Key properties:

• items – list of DropdownMenuItem widgets
• value – currently selected value
• onChanged – callback when selection changes
• hint – placeholder when no value selected
• icon – custom dropdown icon
• isExpanded – makes dropdown full width🔹 Common use cases:

✅ Selecting categories
✅ Choosing country/language
✅ Filter options
✅ Form inputs
✅ Settings selection

💡 DropdownButton is perfect when you need a compact and user-friendly way to choose one option from multiple choices.

data.name: Day 38 - DatePicker
data.description:
DatePicker
The DatePicker in Flutter allows users to select a date using a material design calendar dialog. It is commonly used in forms, booking apps, and profile details.

🔹 What does DatePicker do?

• Opens a calendar dialog
• Allows single date selection
• Supports date range limits
• Returns selected date

🔹 Key parameters (showDatePicker):

• context – build context
• initialDate – default selected date
• firstDate – earliest selectable date
• lastDate – latest selectable date
• onDatePickerModeChange – optional mode listener
• builder – customize theme

🔹 Common use cases:

✅ Booking systems
✅ Date of birth selection
✅ Event scheduling
✅ Form inputs
✅ Reminders & planners

💡 DatePicker is perfect when you need a clean and user-friendly way to select dates in your Flutter app.

data.name: Day 39 - TimePicker
data.description:
TimePicker
The TimePicker in Flutter allows users to select a time using a material design clock dialog. It is commonly used in scheduling apps, reminders, alarms, and booking systems.

🔹 What does TimePicker do?

• Opens a clock-style dialog
• Allows hour & minute selection
• Supports 12h & 24h formats
• Returns selected time

🔹 Key parameters (showTimePicker):

• context – build context
• initialTime – default selected time
• builder – customize theme
• helpText – dialog title text
• confirmText – confirm button text
• cancelText – cancel button text🔹 Common use cases:

✅ Alarm & reminder apps
✅ Meeting scheduling
✅ Booking time slots
✅ Delivery time selection
✅ Event planning

💡 TimePicker is perfect when you need a clean and user-friendly way to select time in your Flutter app.

data.name: Day 40 - Progress Indicator
data.description:
Progress Indicator
The Progress Indicator in Flutter is used to show the progress of an ongoing task such as loading data, downloading files, or processing actions.

Flutter provides two main types:
• LinearProgressIndicator
• CircularProgressIndicator

🔹 What does Progress Indicator do?

• Shows loading state
• Indicates task completion progress
• Improves user experience
• Prevents user confusion during async tasks

🔹 Key properties:

• value – progress value (0.0 to 1.0)
• backgroundColor – track color
• color – progress color
• strokeWidth – thickness (circular)
• minHeight – height (linear)🔹 Common use cases:

✅ API loading
✅ File uploads/downloads
✅ Form submission
✅ Authentication process
✅ Background processing

💡 ProgressIndicator is perfect when you need to visually communicate loading or task completion status in your Flutter app.
